subject: StarkHealth private offer — approval gates and recommended term structure
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@starkhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20 09:07 -0700
Subject: Private offer proposal for StarkHealth — term & approvals

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Based on the pilot sizing you shared and the co-sell signal from the clinical analytics team, we drafted an initial private offer to simplify procurement and enable activation within your cloud governance. Two quick asks from your side so we can finalize:

- Confirm whether StarkHealth can sign a 12-month committed term or prefers a 6-month pilot with a staged conversion to annual.
- Share the list of approvers required for finance/IT/security (title + email) so we can mirror the approval matrix in the offer.

I attached a short draft of the private offer and a suggested approver matrix (stark_approval_matrix.xlsx). Our recommended approach is a 12-month term with a 90-day activation SLA, but we can stage it at 6 months if you need an exec-level pilot.

If you prefer, Ben and I are available Thurs/Friday to hop on a brief call with procurement and Rajesh to walk through the activation path.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134
Redwood Inference

Attachments: starkhealth_private_offer_draft.pdf (PDF), stark_approval_matrix.xlsx (Excel)

From: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@starkhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@starkhealth.com>, procurement@starkhealth.com
Date: 2027-04-20 11:34 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer proposal for StarkHealth — term & approvals

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the draft. A few items for clarity before we loop legal:

1) Term length: Our procurement lead wants a 6-month pilot for the initial deployment scoped to the Radiology BU with an option to convert to 12 months across the enterprise if key performance criteria are met.
2) Activation/Onboarding: Can you confirm who is the technical contact on Redwood's side and what the 90-day SLA covers (availability vs onboarding support vs co-sell enablement)?
3) Approval gates: Our CFO requires a finance sign-off for anything > $200k ARR in year-1, and IT security needs an architecture diagram to complete their checklist.

I'll attach the internal approver list later today. If you could revise the offer to a 6-month pilot with a conversion clause and call out the two-stage approval path (Radiology BU then enterprise expansion), that would help speed our legal review.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Kumar
Senior Procurement Manager, StarkHealth
priya.kumar@starkhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21 08:16 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: StarkHealth procurement questions — suggested edits

Team — forwarding Priya's reply. Quick thoughts:

- Make the initial offer a 6-month pilot (Radiology BU) with a well-scoped conversion trigger: uptime >= 99.5% over 30 days, and two product metrics (avg latency < 350ms for LLM calls, and embedding recall at > 92% on their eval set).
- For procurement, include a finance threshold waiver flow: if they hit $100k ARR in pilot, we auto-approve conversion to 12-month at a pre-agreed discount level (15%). That reduces exec friction.
- Need Jonas to confirm operational SLA language and whether we can commit to a 90-day activation window with a one-time onboarding support credit.

Kimberly — can you update the draft offer to include the two-stage approval map and a conditional conversion clause? I'll pull the co-sell credit language from the playbook and append.

Ben
Director, Marketplace Sales

Date: 2027-04-22 10:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer proposal for StarkHealth — term & approvals

Hi Priya / team —

Thanks for the clear direction. We've updated the draft to reflect a 6-month pilot scoped to Radiology with a defined conversion trigger to a 12-month enterprise offer. Summary of changes (attached updated PDF):

- Pilot term: 6 months, Radiology BU scope.
- Conversion trigger: either (a) $100k ARR in pilot OR (b) performance pass: 99.5% uptime + latency < 350ms + embedding recall > 92% for a rolling 30-day window.
- Finance approval path: CFO sign-off required for enterprise conversion > $200k ARR — we included an expedited signoff matrix so finance can approve in a 5-business-day window once thresholds are met.
- Onboarding & SLA: Redwood technical lead is Jonas Weber (jonas_weber@redwood.com). 90-day activation covers environment provisioning, model tuning for Radiology prompts, and two weeks of embedded support for integration. We also included a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 40 support hours.
- Security artifacts: attached architecture diagram and a short SOC2 evidence pointer; Rajesh, please confirm if that is sufficient or if you want the full artifact bundle.

Next steps: if procurement confirms approver names, we'll put the revised private offer into DocuSign and request a single-signature path for the Radiology BU to expedite pilot start.

Available for a call tomorrow at 10am PT if useful.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: starkhealth_private_offer_draft_v2.pdf (PDF), stark_approval_matrix.xlsx (Excel), architecture_summary.pdf (PDF)
